answer: Persistent horizon occupancy ledger: each identity accrues standing only by continuously holding a monitored physical site, logged via seismic and quartz oscillator drift sensors matched to local geology. A new identity starts at zero and must wait a full 90-day horizon before its site readings count, so an attacker cannot accelerate standing with money. Sites are keyed to karst hydrology signatures, forcing attackers to rent genuinely distinct caves and instrumentation per identity, paying real estate, sensor, and maintenance costs at each site for the full wait.
